primitives.name: Judge-Timekeeper Coordination
primitives.verbatim_quote: 286 WALTER CAMP'S BOOK OF COLLEGE SPORTS XXI Each university shall name two judges and one timekeeper — one of these judges to be located at the finish; the other, with the timekeeper, to accompany the referee.
primitives.assumptions: Each judge-timekeeper pair operates under independent observation protocols with synchronized temporal reference.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When J_f and J_c fail to maintain consistent communication or T cannot verify flag drop timing.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a distributed consensus protocol where J_f and J_c form a local voting node, T acts as a timestamp oracle, and referee serves as a global synchronizer.
layer2.telemetry: Flag drop latency variance and cross-check agreement rate

primitives.name: Neutral Arbitration Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: The appointment of the judges and timekeepers shall be reported to the referee when made.
primitives.assumptions: Arbiter is functionally independent and possesses no institutional bias toward either competing team.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D_{ij} = true and A_n fails to resolve conflict within 10 seconds post-finish.

layer2.mapping: Kernel of a conflict resolution algorithm derived from majority vote logic with an external neutral authority.
layer2.telemetry: Arbitration delay and dispute resolution success rate

primitives.name: Flag Signal Synchronization
primitives.verbatim_quote: XXIII Each of the two judges at the finish shall be provided with a flag of his college color, which he shall drop as a signal to the timekeepers when the boat of his college crosses the finish-line.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_i': 'flag of college i (dimensionless)', 'S_i': 'signal event from F_i (boolean)', 'T_i': 'time of S_i (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Signal events are timestamped and transmitted instantaneously to timekeepers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S_i occurs but T_i cannot be verified due to occlusion or misalignment.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a sensor fusion model where F_i represents a binary event detector and T_i denotes a synchronized timestamp.
layer2.telemetry: Signal-to-timestamp alignment error and flag visibility duration

reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives form a hierarchical system of race officiating where judge-timekeeper coordination ensures local data collection, neutral arbitration resolves disputes, and flag synchronization provides temporal anchoring. These components interact via a ternary protocol: J_f and J_c observe independently, T records timestamps, and A_n acts as a tiebreaker. The system exhibits dualities in redundancy (two judges per location) and duality in decision-making (local vs. neutral authority). Failure modes include communication breakdowns between J_f and T, or A_n's inability to resolve disagreements. Temporal coherence is enforced through synchronized flag drops and timestamped signals. The system's robustness depends on the independence of each actor and the integrity of the flag mechanism. In adversarial contexts, the referee’s pre-race course inspection mitigates physical hazards, while eligibility rules ensure fair competition. The interplay between these elements creates a dynamic network of observers and validators, forming a resilient yet deterministic framework for collegiate rowing race adjudication.
